subject.title: feat: contextual group activation — LLM-driven peeking/engaged state machine

question: Should OpenClaw support LLM-driven contextual activation for unmentioned group messages, and if so should that contract live as a shared channel/plugin SDK seam or as channel-specific core behavior?
rationale: The request changes when shared-room content reaches model providers, adds durable config/state/logging surfaces, and crosses Telegram, WhatsApp, plugin, session-state, and security boundaries; automation cannot choose that product and privacy contract safely.

options.title: Design a shared activation contract
options.body: Create a default-off cross-channel contract with explicit privacy, provider, logging, state, and fallback semantics before channel integrations.

options.title: Narrow to related tracks
options.body: Defer the full peeking/engaged design and pursue the narrower attention-window, per-mention routing/context, or passive hook issues separately.

options.title: Reject ambient LLM peeking
options.body: Keep requireMention, always-on groups, and passive room context as the supported safety model, and document contextual peeking as out of scope for core.

recommendation.title: Design a shared activation contract
recommendation.body: Create a default-off cross-channel contract with explicit privacy, provider, logging, state, and fallback semantics before channel integrations.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history signal on shared group activation, channel docs, and mention-policy boundaries.
